## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** pakcage in R.

There are tones of graphics packages in R (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot2

We can use the in-build data frame `cars` to play with plotting:
```{r}
head(cars)
```


```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now with ggplot:
First install with `install.packages()'

> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot")` in my quarto document as it is re-installed every time the report is rendered

Every time I want to use functions from given packages, I need to load the package with a `library()` call:
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```
Every ggplot needs at least 3 things:

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data = cars) +
	aes(x = speed, y = dist) + 
	geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Speed (MPH)",
       y="Stopping Distance(Ft)",
       title="Stopping Distances")
```

## Gene Expression Plot

Read the data from online:
```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

plot:

```{r}
p <- ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col = State) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "grey", "red")) + 
  labs(x = "Control",
       y="Treatment",
       title="Gene Expression Changes Upon Drug Treatment",
       subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitors from Novo") +
  theme_bw()
p
```

We can install extra packages with `install.packages()` like theme packages (for fun) or actually useful ones like **patchwork** for combining plots

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
      p4
```

```{r}
p1/p2/(p3|p4)
```

```{r}
p +
  facet_wrap(~State)
```


>Q. How many genes are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

>Q. How many are "up" regulated

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

```{r}
sum(genes$State == "up")
```

>Q. What percentage of genes are "down" regulated?

```{r}
total_genes <- nrow(genes)
total_down <- sum(genes$State == "down")
ans <- round(total_down/total_genes * 100, digits = 2)
ans
```

The percentage of down-regulated genes is `r ans`%.

## GapMinder data

Famous gapminder dataset
```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

> Q. How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
head(gapminder)
```

## Plotting GDP vs Life Expectancy 

```{r}
continent_plot <- ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, color = continent) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2)
continent_plot
```

```{r}
continent_plot + facet_wrap(~continent)
```

Histograms of gapminder:
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill = continent)+
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

and a boxplot:

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, y = continent, fill = continent)+
  geom_boxplot()
```
